open_points.subject: ServicePrincipal creation status
open_points.text: “status: PrincipalStatus (active | disabled)” and “Lifecycle candidate: active ↔ disabled” do not say which status a newly created principal receives or whether the administrator chooses it.
open_points.question: Is a ServicePrincipal created active, created disabled, or created in a caller-selected status?
options: Every new principal is disabled until a separate enable action.
The creating administrator selects active or disabled.

witness.initial: An active administrator is authorized to create service principals.
events: The administrator creates an estimate-producer ServicePrincipal.
outcomes: The new principal is active and can authenticate after a credential is issued.
The new principal is disabled and must be enabled before it can authenticate.
witness.observer: The administrator and the producer integration

open_points.subject: ServicePrincipal name uniqueness
open_points.text: “name: str” is described as a human-readable source name, but the text does not say whether equal names are permitted or identify any uniqueness boundary.
open_points.question: May two ServicePrincipal entities have the same name, and if not, is uniqueness global or scoped by source_type?
options: Names may repeat; service_principal_id alone identifies a principal.
open_points.default_guess: Allow duplicate names because identity is service_principal_id.

witness.initial: One active ServicePrincipal named “PresuPro” already exists.
events: An administrator creates another estimate_producer named “PresuPro”.
outcomes: A second distinct principal is created with a different service_principal_id.
Creation is refused because the name is already in use.

open_points.subject: Credential issuance while a ServicePrincipal is disabled
open_points.text: “re-enabling restores none of them, so a re-enabled principal needs a newly issued credential” does not say whether that credential may be issued while the principal is disabled or only after it is re-enabled.
open_points.question: Can an administrator issue or rotate credentials for a disabled ServicePrincipal, and if so, does such a credential become usable when the principal is re-enabled?
options: Credential issuance is refused while disabled; re-enable first, then issue.
A credential may be issued while disabled and becomes usable upon re-enablement.
A credential may be issued while disabled but is immediately revoked or otherwise never becomes usable.
open_points.default_guess: Require re-enablement before issuing a new credential.

witness.initial: A ServicePrincipal is disabled and all credentials that existed at disablement are revoked.
events: An administrator issues a new credential while the principal remains disabled.
The producer presents the newly issued credential.
outcomes: Issuance while disabled was refused, so the producer still has no usable credential.
Issuance succeeded and the credential becomes usable after re-enablement.

open_points.subject: Timing and atomicity of imported-section linking
open_points.text: The section says imported plans and new sections “must do so before activation so that operators can re-allocate to those sections,” while BudgetActivationResult says it is created only after “activation, section linking, previous-version deactivation, and audit commit atomically.”
open_points.question: Are imported plans and PortalSections linked and persisted before activation, or is section linking performed atomically inside activation?
options: Build and persist the candidate version, plans, and linked/new sections before activation; activation later checks allocations and switches versions.
Perform linking inside the atomic activation operation.
Use a separate pre-activation preparation state or model not currently described.
open_points.default_guess: Build the candidate plans and sections before activation, because operators must be able to target them during required re-allocation.

witness.initial: A manual budget is active; an expense is allocated to an old section that has no match in an accepted imported snapshot.
events: A staff member prepares the imported version for activation.
The staff member must re-allocate the expense to a new imported section.
outcomes: Linking occurred before activation, so the new section exists, the expense can be re-allocated to it, and activation can then succeed.
Linking occurs only atomically during activation; the new section does not yet exist for re-allocation, while activation is refused because the old allocation is unresolved.
witness.observer: The operator attempting the transition and viewers waiting for the new budget
